title_en: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra Australia Launch: Everything You Need to Know, Specs and Local Pricing - IGN
body_en:
Take note of the following, my fellow fans of fine tech (and maybe take that note with a generously included S Pen). Samsung’s Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra launches in Australia on 22 October 2026, starting at $2,299. Its headline features include a 14.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display, a MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, an 11,600mAh battery and the aforementioned S Pen. Samsung is also bundling software offers advertised at more than $539 in combined value, making the tablet worth a closer look for anyone considering a premium device for work, study or creative projects.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is built around a mighty simple idea: give folks plenty of screen real estate and software flexibility to tackle several jobs, thus removing the need to go full octopus and constantly reach for other devices. Its remarkably thin design helps make this large display solution more portable, while multitasking tools and AI features broaden its appeal beyond streaming and browsing.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra will be available in Australia from 22 October in Grey, with Wi-Fi and 5G configurations.
Please refer to Samsung.com.au for full product and feature details, terms and conditions.
The starting price covers the entry configuration, with higher storage options available for people who wish to squirrel away larger collections of media, games or creative projects on the tablet. You can even super-size and use the microSD card slot to expand storage, too.
See Samsung Australia's Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra page for local purchasing details.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra’s defining feature is its 14.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display. With a 120Hz refresh rate, 2960 x 1848 resolution and advertised peak brightness of 1,600 nits, the screen is designed for everything from detailed creative work to high-definition entertainment.
Samsung’s Vision Booster technology adjusts the display’s brightness and contrast to suit surrounding lighting conditions. That should be particularly useful when moving between indoor workspaces and brighter environments.
Despite the generous screen dimensions, the tablet measures just 5.1mm thick and weighs 692g in its Wi-Fi configuration. The large display gives users room to keep multiple applications visible, while the slim chassis makes the device easier to slip into a bag between meetings, classes or trips.
An 11,600mAh battery is rated for up to 23 hours of video playback under Samsung’s stated conditions. The tablet supports 45W charging, although the charging adapter is sold separately. Its also been tested to IP68 lab test standards.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra runs Android 17 with Samsung’s One UI 9 interface, bringing Galaxy AI features and multitasking tools into the same workspace.
Multi Window supports three simultaneous app views. That means users can follow an online tutorial, take notes and consult reference material without repeatedly switching between applications. Note Assist can help summarise and organise information, while Gemini provides AI assistance for research and everyday tasks.
Gemini Notebook offers another way to organise material, bringing together information and helping users work through their notes and reference content. Together, these tools are intended to make the tablet useful for more involved tasks, rather than simply providing a larger surface for mobile apps.
Samsung DeX adds a desktop-style interface with a taskbar, resizable windows and drag-and-drop support. Combined with an optional keyboard accessory, it provides another way to approach document work and multitasking. As to whether it can replace a laptop, I reckon that’ll depend on the applications and workflows involved. But it sure seems viable, generally speaking.
Alternatively, if productivity is the very last thing on your mind, the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra features powerful internal components tailored for high-end mobile gaming. Driven by the 3nm MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, it effortlessly runs demanding titles like Genshin Impact at a smooth 60 frames per second.
Up to 16GB of LPDDR5X RAM prevents background lag, while an advanced 3D vapor chamber ensures excellent thermal management during extended play. Backed by that expansive 14.6-inch 120Hz Dynamic AMOLED 2X display and a massive 11,600mAh battery, what’s here should deliver the sustained power needed for an immersive, top-tier portable gaming setup.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra includes an S Pen in the box, valued at $129 in Samsung’s offer breakdown. The stylus supports handwriting, annotation and drawing without requiring a separate purchase.
Eligible new devices also qualify for a collection of software offers with a combined advertised value of $539.90:
● S Pen : $129, included in the box.
● Google AI Pro : Six months, valued at $197.94.
● Adobe Photoshop premium access : Four months, valued at $143.96.
● Notability Plus : Six-month trial, valued at $69.
Photoshop provides image-editing tools, including AI-assisted features, while Notability offers multimedia note-taking, audio synchronisation, transcription and handwriting conversion. Those additions are particularly relevant to users who plan to create, annotate or organise information on the tablet.
Pro tip: The advertised value isn't equivalent to a permanent cash saving. Eligibility and redemption requirements apply, some offers are limited to new subscribers, and subscription charges may apply after promotional periods unless cancelled. So best you check the terms before activating each offer.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra launches in Australia on 22 October 2026, from $2,299. It will be available in Grey through Samsung Australia's, as well as retailers: Amazon, JB Hi-Fi, The Good Guys, Harvey Norman, Bing Lee, Officeworks and Costco, and carriers: Telstra, Optus and Vodafone.
For buyers who need a large display, stylus input and flexible multitasking in a slim tablet, the specification sheet gives plenty to consider. I’d say the key decision is how much use you'll make of those productivity and creative features, particularly at this price. Personally, it’s making a lot of sense to me right now.
Visit Samsung Australia for local availability and configuration details.
